PLoS Med PLoS Medicine PLoS Medicine Public Library of Science 10.1371/journal.pmed.0020124 05-PLME-RA-0071R2 Effects of Caffeine on Human Health A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Smith John A. 1 2 Johnson Jane B. 1 Williams Robert C. 3 Correspondence 1Department of Medicine, Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States 2Center for Health Research, Boston Medical Center, Boston, Massachusetts, United States 3Department of Nutrition, Yale University, New Haven, Connecticut, United States *To whom correspondence should be addressed. E-mail: rwilliams@yale.edu 18 04 2005 2 4 e124 e132 Smith et al. 2005 This is an open-access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License Background

Caffeine is one of the most widely consumed psychoactive substances in the world.

Methods and Findings

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining the effects of caffeine on human health.

 Conclusions

Moderate caffeine consumption appears to have both beneficial and adverse health effects.

 caffeine meta-analysis systematic review human health Medicine Introduction Caffeine (1,3,7-trimethylxanthine) is a stimulant of the central nervous system. This review examines the evidence for both beneficial and adverse effects of caffeine consumption. Methods Search Strategy

We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials.

Selection Criteria

We included randomized controlled trials and observational studies examining caffeine effects.

 Results

We identified 47 studies meeting inclusion criteria.

Characteristics of Included Studies

Summary of study design and population characteristics.

Study Year Population Outcome
Study A 2003 100 adults Increased alertness
Study B 2004 50 subjects Sleep disruption
Discussion

Our findings suggest that caffeine has complex effects on human health.

Low to moderate consumption may provide cognitive benefits 1, while high doses may lead to adverse effects 2.

 Conclusions

Caffeine consumption should be tailored to individual tolerance and health status.

 Acknowledgments

We thank all participants who contributed to this research.

References Brown T Davis K Cognitive effects of caffeine J Neurosci 2002 15 234 241 Green M Adverse effects of high caffeine consumption Am J Health 2003 8 112 120
